Definition: from G1722 and G3105; to rave on, i.e. rage at:--be mad against.
BiblicalUsage: Paul uses this word against himself, remembering how he was exceedingly mad against the Christians in Acts 26:11, punishing them in every synagogue and chasing them into strange cities.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Paul's honesty here is the point — the man who once raged against the church became its greatest apostle, and no past fury is beyond God's reach.
